synopsis: Model credibility is specific to validated parameter space and configuration; the roadmap should define an applicability envelope and extrapolation rules, and label every simulation result as interpolated or extrapolated [f5072, f10488, f9733, f8016]. Sensor pose needs an explicit validated range, relocation outside it should trigger bridge testing, and repaired machines need a field diagnostic confirming return to the validated state [f7922, f10810]. Important sensor and scene limits remain: neural reconstruction degrades sharply beyond a 1–4 m viewpoint shift, degraded-visibility sensor models are least validated, and on-road nighttime pedestrian avoidance was 0% in 2019 and 60% in 2025 despite shortcomings not revealed by daytime protocols [f241, f7886, f7585]. Mechanical evidence also has narrow scope: published mining stopping tests cover unloaded machines on gradients of 1% or less, cited terramechanics findings come from single-wheel rigs and sand rather than full machines, and common Chrono handling tire models do not work on deformable terrain [f5182, f6012, f8498]. Machine-family claims should identify invariant parameters and bounds confirmed physically, while the physical anchor campaign should test family membership, conservatism and failure regions [f5784, f6416]. Simulation should replace only defined repetitive tests within specified machine, sensor, configuration and environment envelopes, retaining physical boundary tests; weak-model regions must be established empirically, and the brief does not justify a fixed fraction of physical testing to retain [f10910, f10991].

relations.note: Identical statements restricting credibility to the validated configuration.
Both restrict published mining stopping tests to unloaded machines and gradients no greater than 1%.
Both report Chrono handling tire models fail on deformable terrain; the latter names models.
Glossary restates the handling-tire limitation and supported alternatives without naming the tool.
Both report developers' warning that handling tire models cannot represent deformable terrain.
Both require sensor pose as an input with an explicit validated range.
Restricted published stopping tests reinforce the lack of loaded and slope coverage.
Measured-envelope restriction provides a sensor-specific instance of configuration-bound credibility.
Classifying results as interpolation or extrapolation requires a defined validated envelope.
Both require review of claims extending outside validated conditions.
Nighttime performance cliffs support concern about poorly validated degraded-visibility conditions.
Missing condition-specific error data undermines universal fidelity claims and motivates phenomenon-specific credibility.
Physical anchors operationalize family claims by checking membership, conservative bounds and model failures.
Glossary places physical envelope confirmation within a detailed-to-simplified soil-model workflow.
Non-conservative validation results led to restricting use below HIC 840 rather than 1,000.
Validated but non-conservative behavior illustrates why discrepancy records must include non-conservative cases.
Retained physical testing must target empirically identified weaknesses, not an unsupported fixed fraction.
Envelope-limited substitution of physical tests requires documented applicability boundaries and extrapolation rules.
